SkyBridge Mobile -- Plan Terms, Section 5 (Data Usage)

5.1 Standard plans include a monthly data allowance; usage beyond the allowance is
throttled to 128kbps for the remainder of the billing cycle, unless the customer has
purchased a Data Boost add-on.
5.2 Data Boost ($10 per 2GB block) must be purchased BEFORE the allowance is exceeded.
Purchasing it after throttling has already begun does not lift the throttle until the
next billing cycle.
5.3 International roaming data is billed separately at $0.05/MB and does not count toward
the domestic monthly allowance, unless the customer has the Global Pass add-on, which
pools up to 5GB of roaming data into the domestic allowance at no extra charge.
5.4 Customers who exceed their allowance 3 or more times in a rolling 6-month period are
auto-enrolled in a mandatory Data Boost for the following cycle, at their own expense,
which cannot be opted out of for that one cycle.
5.5 Military/emergency-responder plan types are exempt from throttling entirely,
regardless of usage.

Account file -- Nadia Kowalski, standard plan (not military), 10GB monthly allowance
Billing cycle: August 1-31, 2026. Nadia reached her 10GB allowance on August 20 and was
throttled from that point on. She purchased a 2GB Data Boost ($10) on August 22, after
throttling had already begun. Nadia does not have the Global Pass add-on. While on a
business trip to Canada in August, she used 200MB of roaming data. This was the first
time in the past six months that her account exceeded its monthly allowance.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Nadia's August 22 Data Boost purchase restore full-speed data for the rest of August?
questions.notes: 5.2: a Boost purchased after throttling has begun doesn't lift the throttle until the next billing cycle.

questions.instruction: What roaming data charge does Nadia owe for her August trip?

candidates.description: $0, pooled for free via Global Pass

questions.notes: 200MB x $0.05/MB = $10.00; she has no Global Pass so it isn't pooled or free.

questions.instruction: Which of the following apply to Nadia's account this cycle?

candidates.description: Her connection is throttled for the rest of the billing cycle
Her Data Boost purchase immediately restored full speed
Her roaming usage was pooled into the domestic allowance
She is auto-enrolled in a mandatory Data Boost next cycle
Her plan is exempt from throttling

questions.notes: Only the throttle-until-cycle-end fact is true; no Global Pass, this is her first overage in 6 months (5.4 needs 3+), and she isn't on a military plan.

5.6 On a Family Plan, the primary account holder's line has unlimited priority data with
no throttling cap. Each additional line shares a pooled 15GB monthly allowance; once the
pool is exhausted, all additional lines are throttled together (the primary line is never

pool. Unlike the standard-plan rule, Family Plan boosts apply immediately, mid-cycle, as

FlexCore Studio -- Class Package Policy, Section 3

3.1 Class packages (5, 10, or 20 classes) expire 90 days from the purchase date; unused
classes after expiry are forfeited with no refund or extension, unless the studio itself
cancels a class the customer was booked into, in which case the expiry date is extended
by the number of days that class was rescheduled, capped at a 14-day total extension.
3.2 Refunds for unused packages are prorated at 80% of the per-class rate for each unused
class, minus a flat $15 processing fee, and are available only within 30 days of the
original purchase date.
3.3 Packages purchased as a gift (registered under a different name than the payer) are
non-refundable under any circumstance, but are transferable to another person once.
3.4 Minors (under 18) may only use a class package while accompanied by a guardian who is
also a current member in good standing.

Customer file -- Renee Abara, 10-class package, $250 ($25/class), purchased for herself
(not a gift) on July 1, 2026. By August 20, 2026, she had used 4 classes and requested a
refund for the remaining 6, and separately asked whether her 8-year-old son could use her
leftover classes on his own while she is not present.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, is Renee entitled to a refund for her unused classes?
questions.notes: The refund window is 30 days from purchase (3.2); she requested at day 50, outside that window, even though the package itself hasn't expired (90-day expiry is separate).

questions.instruction: Under this policy, can Renee's 8-year-old son use her package on his own, unaccompanied?
questions.notes: 3.4 requires an accompanying guardian who is a current member in good standing; he cannot use it unaccompanied.

questions.instruction: Absent any studio-cancelled classes, when does Renee's package expire?
questions.notes: 90 days after July 1, 2026 is September 29, 2026 (31 days in July past day 1, 31 in August, 28 more into September = 90).

Brightwater University Library -- Study Room Booking Policy, Section 6

6.1 Students may book a group study room for up to 2 hours per day, once per day, up to 7
days in advance.
6.2 A no-show (failing to check in within 15 minutes of the booking start) counts as a
strike. 3 strikes within a rolling 30-day period suspend booking privileges for 14 days.
6.3 Cancelling at least 1 hour in advance does not count as a strike. Cancelling less than
1 hour in advance counts as a half-strike (two half-strikes equal one full strike).
6.4 Graduate students may book up to 4 hours per day and are exempt from the strike
system entirely, but are still asked (not required) to cancel unused bookings.
6.5 During final exam period (the last 14 days of each semester), the daily 2-hour limit
is waived for ALL students, undergraduate and graduate, allowing back-to-back bookings
subject to room availability.

Booking history -- Kayla Simmons (undergraduate), trailing 30 days as of September 28,
2026:
Sept 2: no-show.
Sept 10: cancelled 2 hours before the booking start.
Sept 15: cancelled 20 minutes before the booking start.
Sept 22: no-show.
Sept 28: cancelled 10 minutes before the booking start.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, has Kayla accumulated enough strikes to trigger a 14-day suspension?
questions.notes: 1 (Sept2) + 0.5 (Sept15) + 1 (Sept22) + 0.5 (Sept28) = 3.0 strikes, all within the rolling 30-day window (Sept2-Sept28) -> meets the 3-strike threshold.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Kayla's September 10 cancellation count toward a strike?
questions.notes: Cancelled 2 hours in advance, which is at or above the 1-hour threshold in 6.3, so it counts as no strike at all.

questions.instruction: During final exam period, how long may an undergraduate book a study room for in a single day?

candidates.description: No fixed daily limit; back-to-back bookings subject to availability

questions.notes: 6.5 waives the daily limit for ALL students during the last 14 days of the semester, not just extending undergrads to the grad 4-hour cap.

Brightwater University Library -- Visiting Researcher Access, Section 15

15.1 Visiting scholars sponsored by a Brightwater faculty member receive borrowing
privileges equivalent to graduate students (90-day loans), valid for the duration of
their sponsorship letter, up to a maximum of 12 months.
15.2 Visiting scholars are not eligible for interlibrary loan (ILL) services under this
policy, regardless of sponsorship or the equivalence of their other borrowing privileges.
15.3 Sponsorship letters must be renewed annually; access is automatically suspended if a
letter expires without renewal.
15.4 Alumni (former degree-holders) may separately purchase a Community Borrower card
($75/year) with 21-day loan periods and no ILL access, independent of any sponsorship.

sponsorship letter, issued January 1, 2026, covers a 6-month research stay through June

another university. As of August 2026, there is no record of a renewed sponsorship
letter on file for Dr. Lindqvist.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, is Dr. Lindqvist eligible to request the book via interlibrary loan?
questions.notes: 15.2 excludes visiting scholars from ILL regardless of sponsorship or their otherwise grad-equivalent borrowing privileges.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Dr. Lindqvist retain borrowing privileges in August 2026?
questions.notes: Her sponsorship letter covered through June 30, 2026 with no renewal on file; 15.3 auto-suspends access when a letter lapses unrenewed.

questions.instruction: Which access tier best describes Dr. Lindqvist's original (Jan-June 2026) borrowing privileges?
questions.notes: 15.1 grants sponsored visiting scholars graduate-equivalent 90-day loan privileges, distinct from the alumni tier in 15.4.

BazaarHub Marketplace -- Seller Performance Policy, Section 7

7.1 Sellers are rated on late-shipment rate, cancellation rate, and valid-complaint rate,
calculated monthly over trailing 90-day order volume (minimum 20 orders to be rated).
7.2 A late-shipment rate above 5% triggers a warning on first offense, or a 7-day listing
suspension on a second offense within 12 months.
7.3 A cancellation rate above 3% triggers an immediate 7-day listing suspension, with no
warning first, regardless of the seller's late-shipment or complaint standing.
7.4 A valid-complaint rate above 2% results in a permanent ban, unless the complaints
trace to a single defective product batch that has since been recalled by the seller, in
which case only a 30-day suspension applies.
7.5 New sellers (fewer than 90 days on the platform) are exempt from suspension
enforcement for their first 90 days, but still receive warnings, which count toward the
12-month warning history once enforcement begins.

candidates.description: No action; the rate is below the enforcement threshold

City of Rivendale -- Sidewalk Cafe Permit Code, Section 18

18.1 Restaurants may place tables/chairs on the public sidewalk in front of their
storefront provided at least 5 feet of clear, unobstructed pedestrian path remains at all
points. This ADA clearance minimum has no exceptions.
18.2 Permit fee: $200/year for sidewalks 10 feet wide or narrower; $350/year for wider
sidewalks.
18.3 Alcohol service in the cafe area requires a separate Outdoor Alcohol Endorsement
($150/year) and a physical barrier (planters, railing) delineating the cafe boundary.
18.4 Permits are valid April 1-November 30 each year; operating outside this window
without a separate Winter Waiver is a violation subject to permit revocation.
18.5 Corner lots (fronting two streets) must maintain the 5-foot clearance on both
frontages.

Site inspection -- Ristorante Bellavita (non-corner lot), sidewalk 9 feet wide fronting
the storefront. The owner's proposed table layout would leave 4 feet of clear pedestrian
path, per the inspector's measurement. The owner also wants to serve wine at the tables,
planning to use decorative planters to mark the cafe boundary.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, can Ristorante Bellavita's proposed table layout, leaving 4 feet of clear path, be approved?

questions.instruction: Based on its sidewalk width, which permit fee tier would apply to Ristorante Bellavita if it submits a compliant layout?

candidates.description: No fee; not eligible for any permit

questions.notes: The sidewalk is 9 feet wide, which is 10 feet or narrower, so the $200 tier applies (18.2).

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Ristorante Bellavita's sidewalk cafe plans?

candidates.description: The proposed layout meets the 5-foot clearance minimum
The corner-lot dual-frontage rule applies to this site
An Outdoor Alcohol Endorsement is needed for the planned wine service
The planned boundary marker qualifies as a barrier
A standard permit would be valid year-round

questions.notes: Wine service needs the endorsement, and planters qualify as a barrier; clearance fails, it isn't a corner lot, and standard permits run Apr1-Nov30 only.

Solstice Electronics -- Warranty Terms

Section A: New products include a 1-year Manufacturer Warranty covering parts AND labor
for defects.
Section B: Certified Pre-Owned products include a 90-day Manufacturer Warranty covering
PARTS ONLY; labor charges are the customer's responsibility, unless the optional Refurb
Care add-on ($20) was purchased, which adds labor coverage for the same 90 days.
Section C: Products sold explicitly marked "As-Is" carry no warranty of any kind,
including no parts coverage, regardless of any defect discovered, except where required
by non-waivable statutory consumer protection law, which is outside the scope of this
policy.
Section D: A third-party extended service plan does not reinstate manufacturer coverage
that has already lapsed; the third-party plan's own terms govern instead.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Priyanka's warranty coverage?

candidates.description: Her claim is within the 90-day coverage window
She purchased the Refurb Care add-on

VoyageGuard Travel Insurance Certificate, Section 9 (Trip Interruption & Missed Connection)

9.1 Trip Interruption reimburses unused non-refundable trip costs and reasonable
additional transportation costs when a trip is cut short AFTER departure for a covered
reason; this is distinct from Trip Cancellation (Section 8), which applies only BEFORE
departure.
9.2 Missed Connection benefit: if a covered traveler misses a connecting flight due to a
covered carrier delay of 3 or more hours on the prior leg, the policy reimburses up to
$500 for reasonable additional expenses to catch up with the itinerary.
9.3 The Missed Connection benefit does not apply if the missed connection was due to the
traveler's own late arrival at the airport rather than a carrier delay.
9.4 Claims under 9.1 or 9.2 must be filed within 60 days of the covered event.

Claim file -- Oliver Kwan, policy #VG-51190

Oliver's outbound flight from Chicago was delayed 4 hours by the airline due to mechanical
issues, causing him to miss his connecting flight to Lisbon. He paid $340 for a hotel and
rebooking fees to catch a flight the next day. He filed his claim 20 days after the event.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, is Oliver eligible for the Missed Connection benefit?
questions.notes: The 4-hour carrier delay meets the 3-hour threshold in 9.2, and the delay was airline-caused, not his own late arrival, so 9.3 doesn't bar it.

questions.instruction: How much can Oliver be reimbursed for his additional expenses?
questions.notes: $340 actual cost is below the $500 cap, so the full $340 is reimbursed rather than being capped or reduced.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, does Section 8 (Trip Cancellation) govern Oliver's claim?
questions.notes: His disruption happened mid-trip after departure (a missed connection), governed by Section 9, not Section 8 which only applies before departure.

questions.instruction: Under this policy, must Hassan repay his tuition reimbursement?
questions.notes: He resigned voluntarily 6 months after completing the course, within the 12-month clawback window (19.2); the layoff exception doesn't apply since this wasn't a layoff.

questions.instruction: What percentage of Hassan's tuition was originally reimbursed, based on his grade?
questions.notes: A B+ grade meets the 'B or higher' threshold for 100% reimbursement; his $2,000 course is well under the $5,250 annual cap, so the cap doesn't reduce it.

questions.instruction: What reimbursement is Elena entitled to for her unapproved course?
questions.notes: 19.3 requires pre-approval before enrollment; unapproved courses get 0% reimbursement regardless of grade, even an A.
